title: Why rewards can actually reduce your motivation
hook: Giving a reward can make someone less likely to do something again.

narration.text: Giving a reward can make someone less likely to do something again.
This surprising effect is explained by Self Determination Theory.
When we feel in control, our intrinsic motivation is high.
External rewards can make us feel controlled, not autonomous.
Our internal drive can then decrease for that specific activity.
Think about a child who loves drawing, then gets paid for it.
The joy of the act might be replaced by the expectation of money.
Have you ever noticed a passion fading once it became a job?

description: Discover how external rewards can sometimes backfire and reduce our natural motivation for tasks we enjoy. This phenomenon, explained by Self Determination Theory, highlights the importance of feeling in control. Learn how this psychological principle affects daily life.
topic: Why rewards can sometimes decrease intrinsic motivation, explaining self determination theory.
